channel.title: Interface Report
channel.description: Independent publication about AI products, agents, design, Human–AI interaction, engineering, startups and SaaS.

item.title: The dashboard-first era is ending. AI analytics is becoming a conversation.
item.description: OpenAI’s new Data agent points to a bigger product shift: analytics is moving from finding a dashboard to asking, inspecting evidence and acting.

item.title: GPT‑6 Astra is not your product. The capability boundary is.
item.description: A stronger model raises the ceiling, but product quality still depends on what the system is allowed to do, how it proves work and where it fails safely.

item.title: The Agents API changes the build-versus-orchestrate decision.
item.description: OpenAI is moving agent loops, context management and long-running execution behind an API. That shifts where product teams should spend engineering effort.

item.title: Agent harness portability is becoming infrastructure, not a nice-to-have.
item.description: Vercel’s AI SDK can now run GitHub Copilot through the same HarnessAgent interface as other coding agents. The abstraction is moving above the model.

item.title: Permission UX is becoming the real AI safety interface.
item.description: As agents touch real systems, the user experience of scope, consent and temporary access becomes as important as the model’s answer quality.

item.title: The new AI trust loop is not answer → accept. It is answer → inspect → challenge.
item.description: Data agents and finance copilots are making evidence provenance part of the interaction. That changes what trustworthy AI should look like.

item.title: Full-duplex voice breaks the old turn-taking model. Your UI has to catch up.
item.description: GPT‑Live‑1 can listen and speak at the same time. That makes interruption, floor control and visible agent state core voice-interface problems.

item.title: Stop making every AI feature a chat box.
item.description: Chat is excellent for ambiguous intent. It is weak for persistent state, comparison and consequential action. AI products need more than one interaction mode.

item.title: A production agent sandbox needs more than isolation.
item.description: Isolation is necessary, but long-running agents also need persistent workspaces, scoped credentials, recoverable sessions and observable side effects.

item.title: Your average latency is lying to you. Tail latency is where AI products break.
item.description: Fresh infrastructure work from Vercel and OpenAI shows the same lesson at very different scales: optimize the slow iona users actually feel.

item.title: AI pricing is becoming a product system, not a price page.
item.description: Usage, outcomes, credits and enterprise contracts are moving too quickly for annual pricing exercises. AI companies need monetization infrastructure built for iteration.

item.title: Your next SaaS customer may be an agent. Is your product ready?
item.description: Agents are increasingly discovering tools, reading docs, provisioning infrastructure and initiating transactions. SaaS products need a machine-usable iona alongside the human UI.

item.title: The AI product interface is becoming a control surface, not a chat box.
item.description: Intent, permission, progress and recovery for agentic products.

item.title: What makes an AI product feel trustworthy before it feels intelligent.
A field guide to agent UX.
item.description: What the interface should reveal, ask and remember.
